tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the case for Overweight stronger than at any time since the row was set and still not taken. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: A now, C prior: healthcare is the defensive the market is paying for, with Medtech capital goods A, Pharma/biotech B, Medtech consumables B and Pharma manufacturing services B. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only) pays large, proven, cash-yielding cases, which is the Pharma/biotech row (B) and Hospitals (B). Held at C because the industry letter adds the same 30% weight to clinical-stage biotech (D, relative strength F) and capex-cyclical medical equipment as to large pharma, no source spoke to pharmaceuticals against medical technology this week, and eleven of the top 40 on the starting score are already healthcare names. Counter-case for B: two readings two months apart at A with the regime's rotation confirmed on every window; for D: a crowded destination. To B if a source carries a healthcare read with the industry's relative strength holding A or B.

Counter-case: three stocks, leveraged property-heavy operators are rate-sensitive.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: Sell signal: CVS Group's relative 200D MA fell 1.23% over the month to the Fri 6-Nov reading, in force until Fri 13-Nov; (1.13%) on 10-Nov.
Easing slowly; on my calculation at a flat market it ends for the 15-Jan-2027 reading, or for 27-Nov at about 1,589p (+15.1%).
Under your one-off in/out link the whole CVS Group holding is sold when its replacement is bought.

items.criterion: SS Sales or SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero AND Stock RS below 50, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end: PT Net Upgrade Breadth was (18%), but CVS Group's Stock RS was 58.
PT Net Upgrade Breadth is now (27%); a Stock RS of 49 or lower at 30-Nov, 7 points below today's 56, gives a sell signal.
CVS Group's Stock RS fell from 62 to 56 in two sessions while its SP was flat and the market rose.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: the Sector RS of Hospitals, clinics and care homes is 60, above 50, though CVS Group's Stock RS (56) is below 70.
That Sector RS fell from 67 to 60 in two sessions.
It has read 50 or more at three Fridays in a row; its August and September peaks fell below 50 within a week.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: CVS Group's relative price is 11.1% below its 52W high, from 12.8% at 30-Oct and 24.7% at 30-Sep.
At a flat market a CVS Group close below 1,164p, 15.6% lower, gives a sell signal at 30-Nov.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: 4-Nov's 1,387.91p is both tranches' highest close since purchase, putting their 30% level at 971.5p, 29.6% below the close.
Stock RS (56) is below 70, so only the price condition is missing; the 971.5p level is far below the 52W closing low of 1,114p.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal: Healthcare's Industry RS read 92 on Fri 6-Nov, 62 points above the line of 30, and is 92 on 10-Nov.
It rose to 92 from 46 on 16-Oct and 86 at 30-Oct; 92 is the highest in 13 months of readings.

adds.criterion: Where CVS Group stands for an add: pulling back or basing; may be retesting or forming a VCP; healthily retesting or breaking out

bullets.text: The first stage, basing at the top of a 12-month base (1,114p to 1,416p), with a 0.6% pause from 4-Nov on dividend-adjusted closes; none of the later two stages.
The Master Dashboard reads basing plausible (3 of 4 tests), pulling back possible (2 of 4), healthy retest possible (3 of 6), volatility contraction patterns 0 of 4.
A close above 1,416p on 1.5x volume, or a light-volume pullback holding a rising MA such as the 20D (1,324.6p).

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Absent: CVS Group last touched an MA on 19-Oct, the 50D, and closed 4.2% above the rising 20D MA on 10-Nov.
It passes four of your six trend-health tests; the absolute 200D MA is flat ((0.03%) over 20 sessions) and the 150D MA sits 0.66% below the absolute 200D MA.
On my calculation the absolute 200D MA turns up by 12-Nov at closes of 1,330p or more, and the 150D crosses above it about 24-Nov.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Partly present: technicals (Stock RS from 25 on 9-Oct to 56 on 10-Nov) and peers (Pets at Home at its 52W high) are rising, though Stock RS lost 6 points in two sessions.
Guidance is unchanged since 24-Sep; sell-side estimates are mixed: FY2027 EPS flat over 3 months, PT Net Upgrade Breadth (27%), Buys 9 to 8.
Like-for-like growth of 3% or more at the 25-Nov annual general meeting, then analysts raising EPS.
Your 2-Nov note (edited 4-Nov) says CVS Group rose "purely (IMHO) on defensive rotation", with a "weak looking 200D MA line"; its section reads "TBD".
It lists CVS Group among the "Secondary" sell signals; your 10-Nov note does not name CVS Group, though it lists the "Defensives trade".

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
